t.E100.agn: In 2010 EFSA set the acceptable daily intake (ADI) for curcumin at 3 mg/kg body weight; it was not found to be carcinogenic in long-term studies. A refined estimate in 2014 showed that intake in high-consuming young children could approach this limit.
t.E100.body: Curcumin is very poorly absorbed from the gut. In patients taking up to 180 mg a day, curcumin was not found in blood or urine but was found in faeces; in those taking 0.5–2 g a day it was barely detectable in blood, and at 4–8 g it was measurable; it was not found in urine at any dose.
t.E100.prod: Obtained from turmeric root by solvent extraction.
t.E100.regx.0: ADI 3 mg/kg; close to the limit in high-consuming young children.
t.E100.summary: A yellow colour obtained from turmeric root. It gives colour to mustard, curry, sauces and confectionery.
